newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pacific Nickel sees Nonoc mine low cost.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Nickel sees Nonoc mine low cost.

text.p: Australian miner Pacific Nickel Ltd, formerly Arboyne NL, said on Thursday it expected the revived Nonoc nickel project in the Philippines to produce about 38,000 tonnes of nickel a year.
In a project update, Pacific Nickel said Nonoc was expected to be a low cost producer, competitive with existing and new projects under development.
Nonoc has been closed since 1986 but the national government, which owned the complex, entered into an agreement with Arboyne in July 1996 to take over the project.
Pacific Nickel said current expectations were for plant throughput of at least 3.4 million tonnes of ore a year.
The Nonoc mine would provide about 2.4 million tonnes, with some ore bought elsewhere in the Philippines.
Average nickel and cobalt grades were expected in the region of 1.4 percent and 0.1 percent respectively, it said.
On expected recovery rates, Nonoc would produce about 38,000 tonnes of nickel and and 1,500 tonnes of cobalt a year.
Pacific Nickel said it was continuing to work towards the main equity raising to fund the major part of the refurbishment of the complex.
Shareholders would meet on Friday, July 11, mainly to approve a further raising of up to US$20 million through the issue of unsecured convertible notes, it said.
Pacific Nickel shares were two cents firmer at A$1.00 at 4.10 p.m. (0610 GMT).
